subtopicTitle: Perimeter of polygons — regular and irregular

cards.front: What is the definition of the perimeter of a polygon?
cards.back: The perimeter of a polygon is the total distance around its boundary. It is found by summing the lengths of all its sides.

cards.front: How do you calculate the perimeter of *any* polygon with $n$ sides, given side lengths $s_1, s_2, \dots, s_n$?
cards.back: To calculate the perimeter of any polygon, you sum the lengths of all its sides. The perimeter $P$ is given by $P = s_1 + s_2 + \dots + s_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n} s_i$.

cards.front: A regular polygon has $n$ sides, each of length $s$. What is its perimeter $P$?
cards.back: For a regular polygon, all sides are equal in length. If there are $n$ sides, each of length $s$, the perimeter $P$ is given by $P = n \times s$.

cards.front: Calculate the perimeter of an irregular quadrilateral with side lengths $5 \text{ cm}$, $7 \text{ cm}$, $4 \text{ cm}$, and $6 \text{ cm}$.
cards.back: The perimeter is the sum of all side lengths: $P = 5 \text{ cm} + 7 \text{ cm} + 4 \text{ cm} + 6 \text{ cm} = 22 \text{ cm}$.

cards.front: A regular hexagon has a side length of $8 \text{ meters}$. What is its perimeter?
cards.back: A hexagon has 6 sides. Since it's regular, all sides are equal. Using the formula $P = n \times s$: $P = 6 \times 8 \text{ meters} = 48 \text{ meters}$.

cards.front: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of length $a$ and a base of length $b$. Express its perimeter $P$.
cards.back: An isosceles triangle has two sides of equal length. Let these be $a$. The third side is the base, $b$. The perimeter $P$ is the sum of all sides: $P = a + a + b = 2a + b$.

cards.front: A rectangle has a length of $12 \text{ units}$ and a width of $5 \text{ units}$. What is its perimeter?
cards.back:
A rectangle is a quadrilateral with two pairs of equal opposite sides. So, it has two sides of length $12 \text{ units}$ and two sides of length $5 \text{ units}$.
Perimeter $P = 12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 2(12 + 5) = 2(17) = 34 \text{ units}$.
Alternatively, $P = 2l + 2w$.

cards.front: If the side lengths of a polygon are given in kilometers, what are the units of its perimeter?
cards.back: The units of the perimeter will be the same as the units of the side lengths. If sides are in kilometers, the perimeter is in kilometers.

cards.front: Provide one real-world application where calculating the perimeter of a polygon would be necessary.
cards.back: Calculating the amount of fencing needed to enclose a rectangular garden, determining the length of decorative trim for a polygonal room, or finding the distance covered in one lap around a track.
